alt: USGS map showing the distribution of principal aquifers across the United States.
caption: USGS principal aquifers of the United States, 2000. Colours identify aquifer systems; the map does not show water-table depth or whether a particular well is confined.

alt: Angular rock blocks cover the summit of Foel Fras in Wales.
caption: Blockfield on Foel Fras, Wales. Physical weathering breaks bedrock into angular fragments without changing its minerals.

alt: A breaking wave curls and foams along the coast at Porto Covo, Portugal.
caption: A breaking wave at Porto Covo, Portugal. In shallow water a wave slows and steepens; its crest eventually breaks.

alt: Fossilised Ogyopsis klotzi trilobite preserved in dark shale.
caption: Ogyopsis klotzi from the Middle Cambrian Mount Stephen Trilobite Beds, Canada. Fossils help correlate and interpret ancient sedimentary rocks.

alt: Glacier ice occupies a steep-sided mountain basin in Denali National Park, Alaska.
caption: Glacial terrain in the Muldrow Glacier area, Denali. Ice erosion enlarges mountain hollows into cirques and sharpens the ridges between them.

alt: A pale specimen of kaolinite from Ixtassou, France.
caption: Kaolinite from Ixtassou, France, is a clay mineral. Clay as a soil texture means particles smaller than 0.002 mm; mineral identity and particle size are different properties.

alt: The Moselle joins the wider Rhine beside the city of Koblenz, Germany.
caption: The Rhine–Moselle confluence at Koblenz, photographed in 1988. A tributary joins the main channel here.

alt: Deep blue Crater Lake fills a broad volcanic depression, with Wizard Island near its western shore.
caption: USGS aerial photograph of Crater Lake, Oregon. Collapse following the eruption of Mount Mazama formed the caldera; Wizard Island is a younger volcanic cone.

alt: Glen Canyon Dam holds back Lake Powell above a narrow river gorge.
caption: Glen Canyon Dam and Lake Powell, Arizona. Reservoir storage and controlled releases alter the timing and size of flows downstream.

alt: Landsat view of the Thames estuary, coastal shallows and offshore wind farms.
caption: NASA Landsat observation of the Thames estuary. The tidal river widens towards the North Sea; pale water reveals suspended material and shallow coastal water.

alt: Fallen leaves and organic litter beneath white beech trees in New South Wales, Australia.
caption: White beech leaf litter at Carowiry Creek, New South Wales. Organic material on the forest floor stores carbon and provides material for decomposition.

alt: Brown coal exposed at Chukurovo in Bulgaria.
caption: Lignite at Chukurovo, Bulgaria. This fossil fuel formed from buried plant material; combustion transfers its stored carbon to the atmosphere.

alt: A bank of cloud spills over a mountain ridge above Cilaos on Réunion.
caption: A föhn cloud wall above Cilaos, Réunion. Moist air rises on the windward side; descending air on the lee side warms as it is compressed.

alt: Aerial view of elongated low hills around Horicon Marsh, Wisconsin.
caption: Drumlin terrain near Horicon Marsh, Wisconsin. The streamlined hills record former glacier flow; they are landforms left after the ice retreated.

alt: A groyne extends across the beach at Tallebudgera Creek on Australia's Gold Coast.
caption: Tallebudgera Creek, Gold Coast, in the 1980s. A groyne interrupts sediment movement along a beach and can change sediment supply farther down-drift.

alt: Crearlagh Burn descends from a higher tributary valley towards a deeper main valley.
caption: The hanging valley of Crearlagh Burn, Scotland. Tributary valleys can be left above a main trough when a larger glacier erodes more deeply.

alt: The sharp summit and steep ridges of Little Matterhorn in Glacier National Park, Montana.
caption: Little Matterhorn, Glacier National Park, USA. Glacial erosion on several sides can leave a sharp pyramidal peak; this is not the Matterhorn in the Alps.

alt: Cloud lies below the summit of Cruach Ardrain in Scotland.
caption: Low cloud beneath Cruach Ardrain. A temperature inversion can trap cool, moist air below warmer air; a photograph alone cannot measure the temperature profile.

alt: Four NOAA surface analysis charts show pressure contours and weather fronts during a North American storm.
caption: NOAA surface analyses during a late-February 2022 storm. Isobars join equal pressure; front symbols identify analysed boundaries between air masses.

alt: Exposed layers of the Scollard Formation beside the Red Deer River in Alberta.
caption: The K–Pg boundary in the Scollard Formation, Alberta, Canada. The rock record preserves evidence of the transition around 66 million years ago.

alt: A raised embankment separates floodwater from farmland beside the Mississippi at Hannibal, Missouri.
caption: Mississippi levee at Hannibal, Missouri, 20 June 2008. This engineered embankment limits inundation; natural levees instead build up from repeated overbank deposition.

alt: A mesquite shrub grows on a mound of trapped sand in the Mojave Desert.
caption: Mesquite in Mojave National Preserve, California. Vegetation traps wind-blown sand and can build a small dune called a nabkha.

alt: MESSENGER global mosaic of Mercury showing its cratered surface.
caption: NASA MESSENGER mosaic of Mercury, 2011. Spacecraft observations reveal the planet's cratered rocky surface; this is a composite, not a single exposure.

alt: A hand pump used to draw groundwater at Perambalur, India.
caption: Groundwater hand pump at Perambalur, India. Abstraction removes water from an aquifer; pumping may lower the water level around a well, which is measured below ground.

alt: Pale pyroclastic deposits fill the Marella River valley below Mount Pinatubo.
caption: USGS photograph of Pinatubo's Marella River valley, 1 July 1991. These are deposits left by pyroclastic flows, not a view of a flow in motion.

alt: Graw DFM radiosondes and a radio receiver arranged on a table.
caption: Balloon-borne radiosondes transmit measurements of the atmosphere. Profiles of temperature, humidity and pressure help locate inversions and estimate lapse rates.

alt: A reverse fault offsets contrasting mineral layers in a rock sample from the Stillwater Complex, Montana.
caption: Reverse fault in layered igneous rock from Montana's Stillwater Complex. Trace matching layers across the break: the hanging wall moved up relative to the footwall.

alt: Tall orange sand dunes under a clear sky at Sossusvlei, Namibia.
caption: Sossusvlei dunes, Namib Desert. Wind transports loose sand by surface creep and saltation; the dunes record accumulated transport rather than individual grain paths.

alt: The isolated rock stack Hvítserkur rises from shallow coastal water in northwestern Iceland.
caption: Hvítserkur, Iceland. This isolated coastal rock illustrates a stack, with openings cut through its base.

alt: USGS scientists install a field seismometer at Sabana Yeguas, Puerto Rico.
caption: USGS seismometer installation at Sabana Yeguas, Puerto Rico, 10 January 2020. Recorded ground motion distinguishes P, S and surface-wave arrivals; the photograph shows the measuring instrument.

alt: Turquoise water fills the steep-sided Bimmah sinkhole in Oman.
caption: Bimmah sinkhole, Oman. Dissolution and collapse in soluble rock can create closed depressions called dolines.

alt: Melting snow patches and a stream near Fourth of July Lake in Idaho's Sawtooth Mountains.
caption: Snowmelt near Fourth of July Lake, Idaho. Seasonal melting transfers stored snow water into streams, soils and groundwater.

alt: Photographs of clay samples comparing grey reduced material and oxidised reddish material.
caption: Real clay samples showing contrasting redox conditions. Prolonged saturation restricts oxygen, often producing grey gley colours; oxidation can produce reddish mottles.

alt: A soil profile on the Karelian Isthmus with a dark surface, pale leached layer and browner subsoil.
caption: Podzolic soil on the Karelian Isthmus. The pale E horizon has lost material by eluviation; material may accumulate in the B horizon below.

alt: Calcite stalactites hang from the roof of a cave on Mount Kyllini, Greece.
caption: Stalactites in a cave on Mount Kyllini. Dissolved calcium carbonate is deposited as water drips and loses carbon dioxide.

alt: Microscope photograph of leaf epidermal cells and stomatal pores under drought conditions.
caption: Leaf epidermis viewed through a microscope. Stomata regulate gas exchange and water-vapour loss; transpiration is one part of evapotranspiration.

alt: The broad conical slopes of Mount Fuji rise beyond Lake Kawaguchi in Japan.
caption: Mount Fuji from Lake Kawaguchi, Japan. Repeated eruptions built a stratovolcano with layers of lava and fragmental deposits.

alt: An SDO observation of the solar photosphere showing a large dark sunspot group.
caption: NASA SDO observation of active region AR 12192 in 2014. Sunspots are cooler areas of the photosphere; the orange display colour is image processing.

alt: An exposed bank of poorly sorted glacial sediment containing stones of several sizes.
caption: A natural exposure of glacial till. Ice deposits a mixture of grain sizes directly, often without the sorting produced by flowing water.

alt: Aerial photograph of the Giens peninsula joined to the coast by two narrow sediment barriers.
caption: Giens, near Hyères, France. The double tombolo connects the peninsula to the mainland through two sediment-built barriers.

alt: A USGS groundwater observation station in Stephen C. Foster State Park, Georgia.
caption: USGS observation well in Stephen C. Foster State Park, Georgia. Instruments record groundwater levels; the water table itself lies beneath the surface.

alt: Weather instruments inside the enclosure at Charterhall in the Scottish Borders.
caption: Charterhall weather station, Scotland. Standardised instruments measure local conditions; climate describes their statistics over many years.

alt: Long, wind-eroded rock ridges rise above the desert at Dunhuang, China.
caption: Yardangs at Dunhuang, China. Persistent wind erosion shapes elongated ridges in relatively soft rock or sediment.
